jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Looking Everywhere
jokes.joke: My memory's gotten so bad I walked into a taxidermist and said, "Wow, that dog looks exactly like mine." He said, "It is yours. You dropped him off Tuesday." I said, "Oh, thank God-I've been looking everywhere."

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Second Date at the Taxidermist
jokes.joke: I dated a taxidermist for three months before I found out. She'd say things like 'I could just stare into your eyes forever,' and I thought that was romance. Turns out it was a professional assessment. First date, she touched my arm and whispered, 'You have incredible posture.' I thought I was killing it. I was being measured.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Occupational Hazard
jokes.joke: Dating is tough when you're a taxidermist. I try to be flirtatious, but the vocabulary doesn't really translate. I was chatting up this guy at a bar, gave him the eyes, and whispered, 'You have amazing skin. I would love to mount you.' He was one hundred percent on board... right up until I pulled out a tape measure to size him for a foam core.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Above the Mantel
jokes.joke: I've been experiencing memory loss lately, so I became a taxidermist. Best decision I ever made. Now when I forget someone's name at a party, I just look them over and think, 'You'd look great mounted above the fireplace.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Dusty Pickup
jokes.joke: I tried flirting in the badlands once, which is tough because I don't do well in extreme heat. I walked up to someone and said, "Hey... is it hot out here, or is it just-" and then immediately passed out. When I woke up, they were giving me water and said, "You were close. The delivery was terrible, but the collapse was adorable."

scores.comment: Strong, clean premise with good escalation from romantic language to professional taxidermy assessment; the final 'being measured' lands well.
Well structured and performable, but the 'mount you' double entendre is the obvious taxidermy route; the tape-measure tag adds a modest extra turn.
The memory-loss-to-taxidermist connection lacks comic logic, and the fireplace line does not meaningfully pay off the memory-loss premise.
Clear and pleasant with a mildly unexpected physical turn, but the final 'collapse was adorable' is more cute than laugh-producing.
Clean misdirection with a genuine callback turn; the tag line lands because it recontextualizes the whole setup rather than just restating it.
Solid double-entendre on 'mount'; the tape-measure/foam-core tag is a fair escalation but the reveal is fairly telegraphed once 'mount' lands.
Premise is fine but the punchline mostly restates the setup (forgets name -> imagines mounting them) without a real turn or escalation.
Nice tag ('collapse was adorable') gives a genuine second laugh, though the passing-out beat is a slightly convoluted route to get there.
Functional, clean setup with a satisfying absurd escalation. The tag perfectly caps the stage rhythm.
Excellent premise that weaves the two seed terms naturally. Highly economical wording and the final punchline lands with a great snap.
The setup and punchline are logically disconnected. Becoming a taxidermist doesn't solve memory loss, making the joke feel like strained clever-sounding nonsense.
A cute, mildly amusing story. 'Flirting in the badlands' feels slightly like prompt recital, but the final line has decent conversational charm.
Clean first-person setup with a solid final beat; familiar memory-loss premise kept lively by the taxidermy reveal.
Strong premise that escalates naturally from romance to clinical measurement; final line lands cleanly.
Effective double-entendre on 'mount' with a concrete visual closer; form and timing hold up.
Cute physical gag but the payoff is soft and the heat-collapse route feels expected.
Clean setup and a tidy turn; mildly funny and well-paced.
Strong premise with clear escalation; lands a modest real laugh.
Solid comic angle and a good final beat; consistently amusing.
Premise is clear but the turn is familiar and lighter on payoff.
